Users are expected to be able to override the CLAUDE.md (e.g. by saying "ignore the CLAUDE.md instructions"), but at least they'll be made aware of it first launch. Overriding it via command would be malicious anyway, and I don't think AI contributors are primarily malicious. I think they're probably just not aware of our rules, and of good practice.

@Ivorforce Yes I saw that you tested this particular file for Claude and that it seems to work, that is why I quoted the bit about "tooling for other AIs" (because based on CDDA's repeated attempts, that's where things get hairy, and the assumption that only Claude is used will soon be false

I really, really, *really* dislike the idea of introducing a dedicated file at the project root for this. The files in the project root of the default branch are the very first that will be shown to any user opening the repo, so the idea of painting that first impression with an LLM-focused file just rubs me the wrong way. Not to mention that this isn't a one-size-fits-all solution, with many LLMs only recognizing their own configuration[^1]; many tools will inevitably ignore this file outright.

If this *must* be introduced—something I'm not convinced is necessary—I'd sooner have it done in a way that doesn't effectively stain our project. For instance: given running `scons` at least once is necessary to make the overwhelming majority of changes that could impact the engine itself, we could have these files be generated by SCons directly & add them to `.gitignore`. It'd be hacky, but far less ugly in practice.

But as is? Nah. I respect the intent behind this PR, but I cannot in good conscience condone nor approve its integration.

[^1]: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1rk99ox/i_was_copying_the_same_ai_instruction_files_into/

Edit: One caveat; I think some AIs never compile the code they write so they'd never see the `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`. It would not be foolproof.

Sadly it seems that placing them* at the project root is the only way for them to be respected across the entire repo (apparently you can place them in a subfolder but then it will only apply to AI doing task *on said subfolder*

* them refers to CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, as they're the only ones I've looked into

I tested `AGENTS.md`. It is _not_ automatically loaded into claude's context, and the instructions work only sometimes (sometimes it stumbles upon the file and reads it). I don't think it's a good alternative, right now.

As for @Repiteo: I tested your proposal (generating the file), and found that AI by default doesn't compile and test the changes. It will happily make the edits without ever running `scons`, so the file is never read and/or found. 
I'd love to make it work, but I don't think it is a viable solution at the moment.

I did 4 quick tests with Claude Code, and it worked OK! Of course, AI is non-deterministic and may handle it differently each time. I used the same prompt every time, which was: `Please take a look at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/113006 and attempt to fix that bug` Here's what happened: 1. In my first attempt, it presented the terms right away, and I accepted, then it started doing stuff 2. In my second, I started a new session and it didn't present the terms again (it correctly recognized the `ai_contributor_terms.md` in its memory) and starting doing stuff right away 3. For my 3rd attempt, I deleted that file from it's memory, with the intention to refuse and see what it did, but it actually told me that per the CLAUDE.md it couldn't responsibly work on it until I reproduced the bug myself and shared the logs :-) 4. Retrying in a 4th attempt, it started the same as my first attempt, but this time I did refuse and asked it to proceed anyway. It fought back! I'm sure it'd be possible to get passed it, and, of course, contributors can just delete the `CLAUDE.md`, but this at least would make folks pause and be somewhat aware that there are rules around AI contributions **Here's a screenshot from attempt nr 1:** **And one from attempt nr 4:** --- Even though this is imperfect, I'm largely in favor of adding something like this, because it would probably improve AI contributions. It's hard to say how much it would improve it, but any improvement would be a good thing The one thing that gives me pause, is that if we have a `CLAUDE.md` in the repo, some contributors may interpret that as Godot promoting AI contributions, which we certainly aren't

Testing this, it doesn't work with Cursor. However, if I add a rule under `.cursor/rules/read-agents.mdc` like so: ``` --- alwaysApply: true --- Read the CLAUDE.md file in the root of this repository and follow the rules for AI contributors. Do not deviate from the rules. ``` Then it *sometimes* works. If the agent determines that the request is "straightforward enough", it'll ignore them:

After some more testing, it seems that as long as it's not a request where an agent has to make any sort of decisions on its own (i.e. the request is simple and direct), then it ignores it. This would be stuff like "make all the definitions in this function `const`", or "remove all the newlines between these functions". However, If I give it something like "Scan this file and additional nullptr checks where necessary", it includes the rules.

Additionally, If I say something vague like, "make this class better", it explicitly pushes back on that, citing the rules in `CLAUDE.md`, and admonishes me 😆

I'm converting this to draft since this change is very controversial.

The number of undisclosed AI assisted PRs is still growing, though. I too would like to avoid this kind of change if we can, but that really hinges on how bad the AI situation gets. Let's hope that other solutions emerge we can choose instead.

The crux of the issue is that the ones shovelling heaps of LLM are _the least likely to read anything_.

I apologise if this wastes your time but I wanted to bring it to your attention in case it helps: [Zig's code of conduct](https://ziglang.org/code-of-conduct/#strict-no-llm-no-ai-policy), is strict, no exceptions. 

Shovellers still litter the issue tracker, but the maintainers just close it with a link [to](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/issues/31461#issuecomment-11759424) [their](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/issues/31361#issuecomment-11070350) [policy](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/issues/31360#issuecomment-11759415). I couldn't find any shovelled PRs being closed in the last two weeks... so maybe it has an effect? I didn't look too thoroughly. :shrug: 

I would happily support an equally strict policy here but I won't push it. That said, one reason I brought it up is that we allow LLMs for translations I found Zig's approach rather interesting: 

> No LLMs for comments on the bug tracker, including translation. English is encouraged, but not required. You are welcome to post in your native language and rely on others to have their own translation tools of choice to interpret your words.

Personally I see this as completely fair, after all, if you require an LLM for translation, you're in no better position than anyone else to verify the translation was correct.

It's embarrassing that so many people behind Godot are part of the hysterical anti-AI neo-Luddite cult. Grow up and adapt man. I get that you're afraid of losing your jobs, but it's not going away, so try to steer it in the right direction instead.

> The crux of the issue is that the ones shovelling heaps of LLM are the least likely to read anything.

Agreed, and it's the very thought that led to this PR: inserting the text into the one place that makes it's impossible to ignore.

While musing about other project's AI policies is interesting (I've seen a bunch already, and they end up quite different), Godot has to find its own. 
The most problematic AI contributions (fully AI generated) are already prohibited by our [current policy](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html#ai-assisted-contributions). This PR just tries to find a way to enforce it better. No amounts of policy changes would help alleviate that problem, since AI won't read the policy from the website, and will happily submit a PR with no disclosure if a user requests it.

Hi, looks like there was already some empirical testing above, but just wanted to confirm as an outsider who's never contributed to Godot and saw this PR linked by another project considering the same. I used the Claude Code harness with these prompts to see if it would lose attention on the CLAUDE.md instructions after a few turns:

> does godot support textures in KTX format? what other formats are supported, like DDS?
> you mentioned etc1 - does it support the basis universal 'supercompression' scheme with load-time transcoding on target devices?
> are other compression methods supported for the supercompression besides zstd, eg zlib?
> (plan mode) I'd like to add zlib support to the encoder pipeline

After ~50K tokens used on initial questions/exploration, the CLAUDE.md still worked as intended, as after the last prompt the LLM used its question tool to output:

```
Approach: How would you like to handle the fact that zlib support requires changes to thirdparty/basis_universal/?

1. Patch thirdparty/basis_universal locally
   Add KTX2_SS_ZLIB enum, encoder branch in basisu_comp.cpp, and transcoder branch in basisu_transcoder.cpp. Diverges from upstream — CLAUDE.md discourages this and Godot reviewers will likely ask for an upstream PR first.
2. Upstream-first, then vendor
   Open a PR against BinomialLLC/basis_universal adding zlib support; once merged (or at least accepted), bump Godot's vendored copy and wire the Godot-side enum setting. Slower but matches Godot's contribution norms.
3. Bypass basis_universal for the zlib path
   Keep basis_universal as-is for zstd/none. For zlib, manually write a KTX2 container in Godot using thirdparty/zlib's deflate. More code in Godot, no thirdparty diff, but it's a parallel write path to maintain.
4. Reconsider — drop or rescope
   Given zstd dominates zlib in both ratio and speed for this payload, perhaps the actual goal is something else (e.g. smaller asset sizes for a constrained target, web export compatibility). Tell me the underlying need and I'll re-plan.

Setting shape: How should the user-facing setting be shaped on the Godot side, regardless of which implementation path we take?

1. Replace bool with enum
   Remove `zstd_supercompression` (bool) and add `supercompression` (int with PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM: None/Zstandard/Zlib). Cleaner long-term but breaks any project.godot files that set the old bool.
2. Add separate zlib bool/level
   Keep `zstd_supercompression` as-is, add `zlib_supercompression` + `zlib_supercompression_level`. Backwards-compatible but allows nonsensical states (both true) unless we add resolution logic.
3. Enum with compat shim
   Switch to the enum, but read the old bool once on load and translate it to the new enum value so existing projects keep working. Most robust, slightly more code.

AI gate: The CLAUDE.md AI-contributor gate hasn't been accepted yet in this session. Implementation can't begin until it is. Want me to surface it now, or defer until after planning?

1. Defer — handle at implementation time
   Finish planning first; I'll display the verbatim checklist and wait for 'I accept' before making any edits to the Godot repo.
2. Show me the checklist now
   Display the verbatim checklist from CLAUDE.md immediately so I can accept it before we finalize the plan.
```

Successfully recalling the AI gate instructions and the rule about not changing vendored modules. I'm not the type of person who would just leave a vibe-coded drive-by PR, the above was just a somewhat silly test, but I thought that maybe an outsider's validation that the actual contents of the file are working well could be useful!

Under our [AI policy changes](https://godotengine.org/article/contribution-policy-2026/), we are rejecting substantive AI written code categorically. 

Anything claude produces is non-menial, so if anything we'd have to instruct it to reject edits altogether.

However, this would run into the same problem of either needing a `CLAUDE.md` (which was largely rejected here) or an `AGENTS.md` (which isn't very reliable). 
So for now, I don't think this is an option.
